title: Mother's Maiden Name (Again)
summary: Chapter 1, Episode One. Six newcomers arrive separately, then spend their first day as candidates together: a medical that flags all six as irregular, an assembly, a lesson and a free period round kit issue, a fool's errand that an old man in a tea house turns into a win, supper, and a night clearing a nest out of the storm drains under the old town. It ends on a signature nobody can explain, and each player choosing where to spend the night.
structure: A school day with a mecha campaign happening round it. Morning: arrival, the medical, the assembly. Midday and afternoon: a lesson, kit issue and a free period, then the city, the episode's one outing and its most important stranger. Evening: the train back, the requisition, supper with Taka. Night: the drains, the first fight, Vetch at the top, and the night's rests.
designRequirement: Give six strangers reasons to act as one before anything is at stake. Plant the blood-screen flag. Put the antagonist in front of them, kind and useful, and let the table draw its own conclusions. Never explain the Watcher, Cicada, the mitflits or the marker.
castingNote: Taka is built to be liked at once, and he matters later. Play him at full warmth. Vetch is the day's engine: every job comes from him, in person.
downtime: None. One continuous day. The night's rests at the end are each player's own choice.

scenes.title: From Up Here
scenes.description: Scene 0. The GM's opening speech over one picture: the world two hundred years on, the rift, the Directorate, the fishing village that became a great city, what a Frame is, and the gate.

authoring.note: Reopened 2026-10-01: rewritten whole in the house style. The 2026-09-22 seal (checklist v5, all passes clear, the Candidate Gate siting confirmed) was for the old version.

scenes.title: The Road In
scenes.description: Scene 1. The acceptance letter, then each character's first moment on screen: how they look, how we first see them, and a small problem on the way in, rolled and told by the player. A violet mark at head height on a wall. They don't meet yet.

scenes.title: Intake Medicals
scenes.description: Scene 2. The six meet in the infirmary queue. Forms, then a private medical with Doctor Mordant, who tells each of them their screen came back irregular. They come out as Section Nine.

scenes.title: Assembly
scenes.description: Scene 3. The whole intake in the drill hall: the anthem, the charter, and the Deputy Director's address on what the Directorate is, how their days run, and its two rules. Vetch collects Section Nine.

scenes.title: School: First Period
scenes.description: Scene 4. Their first lesson, local studies with Ota, for the whole section: the city on a wall map, and the four founders named. What they win or lose shows tonight.

scenes.title: Kit Issue
scenes.description: Scene 5. Uniforms and a hundred and fifty credits of kit each from Nobu's counter. Then Vetch inspects them and hands Section Nine a docket for the city: COMPOUND, LEVELLING, BUBBLE, ONE.

scenes.title: School: Second Period
scenes.description: Scene 6. A free period: natural history, where they learn what lives in the drains, Hulda Brack's workshop induction, or the small-arms range. All three pay off tonight.

scenes.title: The Errand
scenes.description: Scene 7. Into the city with the docket. The instrument makers laugh and send them to Manako, who owns a tea house, was hazed the same way once, and shows them how to win: requisition the real part. A second violet mark on the way.

scenes.title: The Train Back
scenes.description: Scene 8. The island train home at dusk, nothing asked of anyone for twenty minutes, then their paper handed in at the stores before nineteen hundred.

scenes.title: Canteen
scenes.description: Scene 9. Supper in the Long Hall. Taka claims the six as his table. Vetch reads the evening's orders and gives Section Nine the storm drains, Dock C at twenty-one hundred.

scenes.title: The Walk Down
scenes.description: Scene 10. Waders that don't fit, Vetch's one-line briefing at Dock C, and the duty launch across the harbour to the old town.

scenes.title: Flood Tunnel Clearance
scenes.description: Scene 11. The first fight: power the line, clear the feed, and a nest of giant centipedes wakes. Vetch is waiting at the top with their requisition, countersigned by someone called Rand. Then each player picks where to spend the night.

requiredBeats: Each of the six is told alone that their screen came back irregular, and the table can work out it was all of them.
Nobody explains what the screen tests for.
The table hears the four founders' names: Shucks's badge at the medical, then the history lesson.
Vetch is met in person: at the assembly, with the docket, with the night's order, at Dock C, and at the top of the drains.
The Deputy Director tells the intake what the Directorate says it is for, and its two rules: disobeying an order is serious, breaking curfew is not.
An old man in a tea house turns the fool's errand into a win and says one true thing about the Directorate. Nothing in the scene suggests he is anything but kind.
The first school period is a lesson the whole section sits; the second is a free choice of room. What they win or lose in each pays off tonight.
The episode ends with each player choosing their own night's rest.
danglingThreads: Why every acceptance letter this year was stamped BROUGHT FORWARD.
What the blood screen's IRREGULAR box is looking for.
Who Rand is: a countersignature in green ink, and nobody of that name in Medical.
Who the old man in the tea house really is.
Violet marks at head height, seen twice in one day.
Why the six Section Nine cards leave the track blank.
A father on the radio, and his daughter held without charge.
notes:
Every scene is in canon/scenes, in the house style, waiting for Ingram's read.

STANDING RULES FROM THIS EPISODE
1. Vetch is a real, present character, never a voice over a tannoy: every job comes from him in person.
2. Never predict the table's response. State what the scene does.
3. Session length is not a constraint.

THE SCHOOL PERIODS. The first is a lesson the whole section sits (local studies); the second is their own choice of room. Not rolling is free; nothing is announced; failure costs something real. Every payoff lands tonight:
- Local studies: the founders' names on any result; a failure makes them last into the stores, where the handlamps have sold out.
- Workshop: +2 circumstance on panel work in the drains.
- Natural history: the centipedes already known (a free Recall Knowledge); on a critical success, a show of force sends one running.
- The range: +1 circumstance on a first ranged Strike tonight.
- Any critical failure: Fatigued tonight.

THE VIAL. Vetch's docket (Kit Issue) is the hazing. Manako's plan (The Errand) turns it: requisition the real part. It goes in at the hatch (The Train Back), where vials go up to Medical, earns them the drains (Canteen), and comes back countersigned by Rand (Flood Tunnel Clearance). Rand is Shucks's detached right hand; nobody knows. If they file no requisition, Rand countersigns whatever paper of theirs goes in instead, so the ending always lands.

REFUSING AN ORDER. Every order in the episode says what Vetch does if someone refuses. A refusal goes to the Deputy Director the same day, as a beat in The Errand (the docket) or Flood Tunnel Clearance (the drains), on one shared check.

LEVELLING is by milestone, so no scene awards XP. Working out that all six were flagged earns a Hero Point, the same night.

IF IT RUNS TO TWO EVENINGS, the natural break is Vetch's order at supper: end on "Section Nine: storm drain clearance", and start the next evening with the waders.
